data.title: Wheels India Raises ₹250 Crore via Qualified Institutions Placement
data.description:
Wheels India Limited ( (IN:WHEELS) ) has issued an announcement.

Wheels India Limited has raised approximately ₹250 crore through a qualified institutions placement, issuing 1,197,318 equity shares of face value ₹10 each at an issue price of ₹2,088 per share, including a premium of ₹2,078 and a small discount to the regulatory floor price. The placement, approved by the Fund Raise Committee on September 25, 2026, expands the company’s paid-up equity capital from ₹25.67 crore to ₹26.86 crore, modestly diluting existing shareholders while strengthening its capital base and financial flexibility.

The new shares were allotted exclusively to eligible qualified institutional buyers, with details of large allottees and the updated shareholding pattern to be filed along with the listing application as per SEBI’s disclosure norms. By tapping institutional investors via QIP, Wheels India reinforces its market positioning as a compliant, growth-focused listed entity, potentially enhancing its capacity to fund future expansion, manage leverage or pursue strategic initiatives in a competitive automotive components industry.

data.title: S&P Assigns BBB+ Global Rating to Qualitas with Negative Outlook
data.description:

S&P Global Ratings has assigned Qualitas Compañía de Seguros a global financial strength and long-term issuer credit rating of BBB+, both with a negative outlook, aligning the insurer’s rating with Mexico’s local-currency sovereign ceiling. The global assessment complements the existing mxAAA national-scale rating with a stable outlook, framing Qualitas’ credit profile within both domestic and international benchmarks and underscoring its relative strength in the Mexican market.

S&P notes that Qualitas’ capitalization and liquidity allow it to pass the foreign-currency sovereign stress test and be rated one notch above Mexico’s foreign-currency sovereign rating, even as the negative outlook reflects sovereign-level risks rather than company-specific weaknesses. The agency highlights nearly three decades of underwriting experience, leadership in Mexico’s auto insurance segment, pricing expertise and an efficient operating model as competitive advantages expected to support resilient performance and continued outperformance versus peers.

data.title: Fusion Fuel Green to Restate 2025 Financials After Currency and Goodwill Errors
data.description:
Fusion Fuel Green ( (HTOO) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On September 23, 2026, Fusion Fuel Green disclosed that its audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 must be restated due to errors in foreign currency translation of intangibles and goodwill tied to its acquisition of Quality Industrial Corp. The company also identified misclassification of foreign exchange differences and the need to redo its goodwill impairment analysis for that period.

Fusion Fuel Green plans to file an amended annual report with expanded disclosure on the restatement, and currently estimates the corrections will increase its 2025 net loss by about €4.0 million and reduce equity by roughly €3.8 million. Management emphasizes that the adjustments are non-cash, do not affect revenue, cash or net cash flows, and are not expected to jeopardize its Nasdaq listing, though the figures remain preliminary and subject to further audit review.

data.title: Aloro Mining Moves to Semi-Annual Financial Reporting Under Canadian Venture Issuer Relief
data.description:
Aloro Mining ( (TSE:AORO) ) has issued an update.

Aloro Mining Corp. has elected to adopt semi-annual financial reporting, making use of a Canadian securities blanket order that allows eligible venture issuers to move from quarterly to semi-annual disclosure. The company qualifies as a low-revenue venture issuer with a clean continuous disclosure record, enabling it to streamline its reporting cycle.

Under the new regime, Aloro will cease filing first- and third-quarter interim financial statements and MD&A, beginning with the nine-month period ended Sept. 30, 2026. It will continue to publish audited annual results and a six-month interim report, a shift that reduces compliance burden while maintaining key financial transparency for investors and regulators.

data.title: SideChannel Shareholders Approve Significant Capital Structure Reduction
data.description:
SideChannel ( (SDCH) ) has shared an update.

On September 23, 2026, SideChannel, Inc. held a special meeting of stockholders to vote on reducing its authorized share capital for both common and preferred stock. The company sought approval to amend its certificate of incorporation to cut authorized common shares from 681,000,000 to 13,100,000 and authorized preferred shares from 10,000,000 to 1,000,000, a move that significantly tightens its potential equity issuance capacity.

Stockholders representing a quorum of 2,843,743 common shares voted, with 2,680,894 shares in favor, 162,791 against and 58 abstaining, approving the amendment to the certificate of incorporation. Because the main proposal passed, the related adjournment proposal became moot and was not presented, underscoring decisive shareholder support for a leaner capital structure that may impact future financing flexibility and share dilution dynamics.

data.title: SKK Holdings Advances $258.8 Million Rantizo Drone Asset Deal and Names New President
data.description:
The latest update is out from SKK Holdings Limited ( (SKK) ).

On June 22, 2026, SKK Holdings’ shareholders approved the acquisition of substantially all of Rantizo Inc.’s drone-based technology assets used in agricultural spraying, seeding and monitoring, alongside forestry, emergency response and other commercial applications, for a mix of cash and approximately $258.8 million in newly issued Class A shares. The transaction, valued at about $258.8 million plus a modest cash component, will also see the company change its name to Rantizo after closing and issue additional equity tied to a $10 million Rantizo financing, with pro forma figures indicating a sharp increase in goodwill and intangible assets and significant dilution for existing shareholders.

As part of the deal, Rantizo gains board representation and has nominated Marianne McInerney to become executive director and President upon closing, while SKK’s current COO, Ng Chun Seong, will step down from the board but remain in his operational role. McInerney’s background in transportation, mobility and drone policy is expected to support the strategic growth and commercial expansion of the enlarged autonomous aviation business, as SKK’s management presents unaudited pro forma financials illustrating the acquisition’s impact on the balance sheet and capital structure but emphasizing that these figures are illustrative and exclude potential synergies.
